failures.evidence: A linked image in a list item, a block quote or a footnote definition, whose link title holds a line that is an inline HTML tag (, , , ), is stored with that line raw. Go reads the raw line as the title's lazy continuation, so pmdoc's checks pass. The browser editor's engine reads it as an HTML block that ends the paragraph. Real browser (Playwright Chromium against the real server, throwaway spec tester/zz-tester-r8.e2e.ts, log tester/e2e-r8-probe2.log, screenshot tester/r8-probe-defect.png): an issue spec holding '- [![badge](https://ci.example/badge.svg)](https://ci.example/build "a z")' is stored as '- [![badge](…)](https://ci.example/build "a\n\nz")'. The live editor draws the picture in its link, but the past-version view (VersionView reads the stored markdown with the engine) draws '[', the picture, '](https://ci.example/build "a', '', 'z")' as text, and the link is gone. The control title 'a b z' draws in its link in both views. In a block quote the engine reads the whole quote as one paragraph 'z")', so the picture is lost too. differential.sh --base 748e8d952a76 --head 3ee687b6 --corpus tester/corpus-r8 (3,000 seeded fuzz documents) plus corpus-r5/r6/r7/corpus: GATE misreads 10 and 15 engine-misread lost whole-image links (tester/diff-r8-vs-main.log); the minimal corpus tester/corpus-r8min gives 24 lost whole-image links, every one a /// line in a list, ordered list, quote, list>quote, nested list or footnote (tester/diff-min-main-r8). The same defect is at 999f2d4b (9 misreads, 13 engine-misread lost links on the fuzz corpus; tester/diff-r7-vs-main-fuzz.log): continuesParagraph judges a lazy line with Go's block reader, and rawTitleMisread checks with Go's Parse, so neither sees the engine's reading. Red test TestRenderWritesALazyHTMLTagTitleLineSoTheEngineReadsItBack in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/pmdoc/render_test.go, commit 3d0237aa03964a68b5149afd4531c9f5b8bec5c9, fails with `cd packages/envoy && go test ./internal/dispatch/pmdoc/ -run TestRenderWritesALazyHTMLTagTitleLineSoTheEngineReadsItBack` (all 24 rows); a copy passes at 733ebfdb, which wrote those titles .

checked: Equivalence to 999f2d4b, which the architect asked for: it does not hold on the fuzz corpus. differential.sh --base 999f2d4b --head 3ee687b6 over 5,774 documents reports churn 106 and lost fixed points 59, all fuzz documents (tester/diff-r8-vs-r7.log). The rows I read are 999f2d4b over-escaping: it blamed the raw image before the first misread one, where 3ee687b6 keeps those titles raw and both read back in Go. Against main the churn gate is 0. The two 'regressions' against 999f2d4b are the failure above.

76 'lost whole-image link' rows in the fuzz runs are refused at main and at the head alike ('typed block "callout" holds a line continuing a paragraph'): my fuzz context puts unprefixed lines inside a prefixed callout. Not an R2 regression.

Performance risk, not counted as a failure: Render now pays Parse's superlinear cost on one long raw title. A list-item image whose title has 12,500 / 25,000 / 50,000 / 100,000 lines renders in 0.25 / 0.72 / 1.7 / 5.7 s at the head, against 0.3 ms at main and 4.4 ms at 733ebfdb (which escaped it). Main's own ParseForWrite of the same document already takes 0.08 / 0.30 / 1.2 / 4.5 s, so the write path was already superlinear; the head adds that cost to every render of a stored document holding such a title.
Ungated and unchanged: ≫⃒ and ≪⃒ 'lost fixed point of a misread'; the carriage-return rows.
